title: U.S. House · New York's 21st District
area: The North Country: St. Lawrence, Jefferson, Lewis, Franklin, Clinton, Essex, Hamilton, Fulton and Warren counties, plus parts of Saratoga and Herkimer counties in far northern New York.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Republican Elise Stefanik did not seek re-election to the House and is instead a candidate for New York Governor in 2026.

Blake Gendebien defeated Stuart Amoriell in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 64.5%-35.0%. Anthony Constantino defeated Robert Smullen in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary, 59.2%-40.3%; Smullen remains on the general-election ballot on the Conservative Party line.

summary.text: Blake Gendebien is a second-generation dairy farmer and small business owner from the North Country running as the Democratic nominee for this open seat, with a campaign focused on affordability, healthcare access and government reform.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Pennsylvania State University in 1999.
Works as a farmer and small business owner; served as Vice Chair of the Cooperative Board of Agri-Mark.
Served on the Lisbon Central School Board and founded a nonprofit supporting children with pediatric cancer and their families.

priorities.text: Affordability, including repealing what he describes as costly and unnecessary government regulations, supporting fair trade deals and bringing back American manufacturing to lower costs for working families.
Healthcare access in rural communities, including expanding telehealth, lowering prescription drug costs, and opposing cuts to Social Security, Medicare or Medicaid.
Government reform, saying he wants to end the "elected to lobbyist" pipeline and get dark money out of politics.
priorities.quote: I'm committed to cleaning up Washington and I will always be responsive to the voters of the North Country, not special interests.

positions.summary: Says he will protect a woman's right to choose and opposes new regulations imposing total abortion bans, including in cases of rape or when the mother's life is at stake.
Says he will never vote to cut Social Security, Medicare or Medicaid and wants to expand telehealth and lower prescription drug costs.

candidates.name: Anthony Constantino
candidates.currentRole: Founder and CEO of Sticker Mule

summary.text: Anthony Constantino is the founder and CEO of Sticker Mule, a printing and technology company based in Amsterdam, NY, running as the Republican nominee for this open seat on a self-funded campaign centered on immigration enforcement, healthcare cost reform and cutting government spending.

background.text: Founder and CEO of Sticker Mule, a global printing and technology company with more than 1,000 employees.

priorities.text: Says he is self-funding his campaign to be free of special-interest influence and does not ask for donations.
Addressing illegal immigration, citing his fluency in Spanish and stating open borders have caused suffering in the U.S. and abroad.
Healthcare policy focused on innovation and outcomes rather than what he describes as an endless debate over making it free.

positions.summary: Cites illegal immigration as a top concern and says open borders have caused significant harm.
